questions.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}u\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }v\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }w\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }0 \\ x\overset{\,\,\,A\,\,\,\,}{\to }y\overset{\,\,\,A\,\,\,\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

Given the action of the matrices $A-5I$ and $A$ on the nonzero vectors $u,v,w,x$ and $y$ as depicted above, which of the following statements are true?

I. $v$ is a generalized  eigenvector of rank $2$  corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5$ of $A$

II. $y$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $1$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of $A$

III. $u$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $4$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5$ of $A$
questions.worked_solution:
A *generalized eigenvector* ${v}_{n}$ of rank $n$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda $ of a matrix $A$ is a nonzero vector such that

$$
{v}_{n}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{n-1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }…\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }0,
$$

where ${v}_{n-1},{v}_{n-2},…,{v}_{1}\ne 0.$ An *eigenvector* is simply a generalized eigenvector of rank $1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, since 

$$
v\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }w\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }0,
$$

i.e. $A-5I$ maps $v$ to $0$ in $2$ steps, 
the vector $v$ is an generalized eigenvector of rank $2$  corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5$ of $A.$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, since

$$
y\overset{\,\,\,A\,\,\,\,}{\to }0,
$$

i.e. $A=A-0I$ maps $y$ to $0$ in $1$ step, 
the vector $y$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $1$ (a.k.a. an eigenvector) corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of $A.$

- Statement III is false. Since

$$
u\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }v\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }w\overset{A-5I\,}{\to }0,
$$

i.e. $A-5I$ maps $u$ to $0$ in $3$ steps, 
the vector $u$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3,$ not $4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $v$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $v$ is an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1$ of $A$

II. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1$ of $A$

III. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1$ of $A$
questions.worked_solution:
A *generalized eigenvector* ${v}_{n}$ of rank $n$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda $ of a matrix $A$ is a nonzero vector such that

$$
{v}_{n}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{n-1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }…\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }0,
$$

where ${v}_{n-1},{v}_{n-2},…,{v}_{1}\ne 0.$ An *eigenvector* is simply a generalized eigenvector of rank $1.$

First, we compute $A-I:$

$$
A-I=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- Next, we find the image of $v$ under the action of $A-I:$

$$
(A-I)v=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\ne 0
$$

- Since we got a nonzero vector in the last step, we now compute the image of $w$ under the action of $A-I:$

$$
(A-I)w=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0
$$

So, we obtain the following chain of maps:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{v}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{0}
$$

Here, we see that $A-I$ maps $v$ to $0$ in $2$ steps.

Therefore:

$\,$ *$v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1$ of $A.$*

So, the correct answer is "III only."

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 1 \\ 4 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $v$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $v$ is an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2$ of $A$

II. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2$ of $A$

III. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2$ of $A$
questions.worked_solution:
A *generalized eigenvector* ${v}_{n}$ of rank $n$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda $ of a matrix $A$ is a nonzero vector such that

$$
{v}_{n}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{n-1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }…\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }0,
$$

where ${v}_{n-1},{v}_{n-2},…,{v}_{1}\ne 0.$ An *eigenvector* is simply a generalized eigenvector of rank $1.$

First, we compute $A+2I:$

$$
A+2I=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 1 \\ 4 & -9 & 1\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -9 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

- Next, we find the image of $v$ under the action of $A+2I:$

$$
(A+2I)v=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -9 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\ne 0
$$

- Since we got a nonzero vector, we now compute the image of $w$ under the action of $A+2I:$

$$
(A+2I)w=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -9 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}\ne 0
$$

- Again, since we got a nonzero vector in the last step, we now compute the image of $x$ under the action of $A+2I:$

$$
(A+2I)x=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -9 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0
$$

So, we obtain the following chain of maps:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{v}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{0}
$$

Here, we see that $A+2I$ maps $v$ to $0$ in $3$ steps.

Therefore:

$\,$ *$v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2$ of $A.$*

So, the correct answer is "III only."

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $v$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $v$ is an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3$ of $A$

II. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $1$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3$ of $A$

III. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3$ of $A$
questions.worked_solution:
A *generalized eigenvector* ${v}_{n}$ of rank $n$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda $ of a matrix $A$ is a nonzero vector such that

$$
{v}_{n}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{n-1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }…\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }0,
$$

where ${v}_{n-1},{v}_{n-2},…,{v}_{1}\ne 0.$ An *eigenvector* is simply a generalized eigenvector of rank $1.$

First, we compute $A-3I:$

$$
A-3I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- Next, we find the image of $v$ under the action of $A-3I:$

$$
(A-3I)v=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\ne 0
$$

- Since we got a nonzero vector, we now compute the image of $w$ under the action of $A-3I:$

$$
(A-3I)w=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}\ne 0
$$

- Again, since we got a nonzero vector in the last step, we now compute the image of $x$ under the action of $A-3I:$

$$
(A-3I)x=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0
$$

So, we obtain the following chain of maps:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{v}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{0}
$$

Here, we see that $A-3I$ maps $v$ to $0$ in $3$ steps.

Therefore:

$\,$ *$v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3$ of $A.$*

So, the correct answer is "None of the statements are true."
